svg.title: Approve and return the final certificate — instructional mockup
svg.desc: Step-specific guided recreation. Not a genuine screenshot or live result.
svg.text: INSTRUCTIONAL MOCKUP — NOT A LIVE CAPTURE OR RESULT
Approve and return the final certificate
Practice CA server (TLS-CA01) · RHEL 9 Bash terminal · learner@10.90.0.20
RHEL 9 — learner@tls-ca01
COMMAND / FILE CONTENT TO ENTER — PRESERVE CASE
cd ~/tls-ca
openssl req -in incoming/app-v4.csr -noout -verify -subject
openssl x509 -req -in incoming/app-v4.csr -CA intermediate.crt -CAkey intermediate.key -CAserial
intermediate.srl -CAcreateserial -days 90 -sha256 -extfile server.ext -out issued/app-v4.crt
openssl verify -CAfile root.crt -untrusted intermediate.crt -purpose sslserver -verify_hostname
app.example.mil issued/app-v4.crt
cp issued/app-v4.crt public/
chmod 644 public/app-v4.crt
EXPECTED RESULT / SIMULATED CLUE — CHECK YOUR OWN MACHINE
issued/app-v4.crt: OK appears, and the public response file is ready.
FOLLOW THE NUMBERED INSTRUCTIONS IN THE LESSON
1. Inspect the new request on the CA and approve only the intended app.example.mil identity.
2. Sign with the existing intermediate, check the returned leaf and copy it into the response folder.
3. Leave all CA private keys on this separate VM.
No real private key, real certificate result, production access or DoD endorsement is shown.
